q: The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an ____.
e: Electron flow is from low potential to high potential. That flow of charge is an electric current. The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an electric current.

q: In general, an electric current is a flow of ____ from one place to another.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. In general, an electric current is a flow of electric charge from one place to another.

q: The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an ____.
e: Electric current is charge passing a cross-section per second, I = Q/t. The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an electric current.

q: The ____ of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an electric current.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an electric current.

q: Current is a ____ quantity by the above definition.
e: By I = Q/t, current is a scalar. Current is a scalar quantity by the above definition.

q: Suppose that the amount of charge $Q$ passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in time $t$, the current $I$ flowing through the conductor is ____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Suppose that the amount of charge Q passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in time t, the current I flowing through the conductor is I = (Q)/(t).

q: If the number of electrons passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is $n$, the amount of charge $Q$ is ____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the number of electrons passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is n, the amount of charge Q is Q = ne.

q: In the SI system, the unit of electric current is ____ (A) in honour of the French physicist, Andre Ampere.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. In the SI system, the unit of electric current is ampere (A) in honour of the French physicist, Andre Ampere.

q: If the amount of charge ____ passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in 1 second, the current is 1 ampere.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If the amount of charge 1 coulomb passes through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in 1 second, the current is 1 ampere.

q: Therefore, 1 A is equivalent to ____.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. Therefore, 1 A is equivalent to 1 C s^-1. 1 c s^-1 is what this sentence is naming.

q: 1 milliampere (mA) = ____ A.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. 1 milliampere (mA) = 10^-3 A. 10^-3 is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: 1 microampere ($\mu$A) = ____ A.
e: 1 A = 1 C s⁻¹, 1 mA = 10⁻³ A, and 1 μA = 10⁻⁶ A. 1 microampere (μA) = 10^-6 A. 10^-6 is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of ____ from a higher potential to a lower potential.
e: Conventional current follows positive charge from high potential to low. Electron flow is the opposite arrow. The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of positive charge from a higher potential to a lower potential.

q: Hence, the direction of current is ____ to that of the flow of electrons.
e: Conventional current follows positive charge from high potential to low. Electron flow is the opposite arrow. Hence, the direction of current is opposite to that of the flow of electrons.

q: When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce three main effects. They are (1) ____ (2) chemical effect and (3) magnetic effect.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce three main effects. They are (1) heating effect (2) chemical effect and (3) magnetic effect.

q: As an electric current flows through, the ____ wire in the bulb becomes hot and emits light.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. As an electric current flows through, the tungsten wire in the bulb becomes hot and emits light.

q: Practical application of the heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron and ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. Practical application of the heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron and immersion heater.

q: When a current is passed through copper sulphate solution with copper plates A (anode) and C (____) dipping into it, some copper is deposited on the plate C after sometime.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. When a current is passed through copper sulphate solution with copper plates A (anode) and C (cathode) dipping into it, some copper is deposited on the plate C after sometime.

q: The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals and ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals and electro-plating.

q: When a current flows through a coil of insulated wire which is wound round a bar of ____, the bar becomes a magnet and attracts steel pins.
e: When a current flows through a coil of insulated wire which is wound round a bar of soft iron, the bar becomes a magnet and attracts steel pins. Soft iron is what this statement is using.

q: The magnetic effect of current is used in making ____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of current is used in making electromagnets.

q: Electromagnets are used in electrical devices such as electric bell, ____ and electric motor.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. Electromagnets are used in electrical devices such as electric bell, magnetic relay and electric motor.
